content.title: About
content.content: Tortellini are small ring-shaped pasta filled with creamy cheese. This version contains no meat and is served with a light vinaigrette made from olive oil, vinegar, and fresh herbs. Tortellini cook quickly and their delicate flavor makes them popular in both cold and warm salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortellini originate from Italy, where they were traditionally meat‑filled, but vegetarian versions became common in the 1920s.
The creamy cheese filling provides a smooth texture and a subtle tang that pairs well with vinaigrette.
The vinaigrette often includes balsamic vinegar, which highlights the cheese’s flavor.
Tortellini can be steamed, boiled in salted water, or baked in the oven with sauce.
They are frequently served in cold salads during summer because they cool quickly and hold their shape.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: The cheese filling supplies calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Durum wheat pasta and cheese provide both plant and dairy protein for tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Absence of meat makes the dish lower in saturated fat compared with traditional versions.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Durum wheat and cheese contain B1, B2, and B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants in vinaigrette
items.content: Olive oil and vinegar are rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Tortellini made from wheat contain gluten, unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese and prepared vinaigrette can be salty; sodium‑sensitive individuals should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While less fatty, cheese and oil add calories; moderation is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tortellini cold in a salad tossed with vinaigrette, or gently warm them. They pair well with leafy greens, cherry tomatoes, and nuts for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry tortellini in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked pasta and vinaigrette should be refrigerated and consumed within 3 days.
